subtype: Approach: noticing a chore keeps piling up and finding why [Revision]
passage: Every Saturday morning in the village, Lakshman's laundry basket was so full that clothes spilled onto the floor of the veranda. His sister Ankita held her nose and laughed. "How does it always get like this?" Lakshman scratched his head. Instead of complaining, he watched himself for three days. Every evening he dropped his shirt on the chair beside the cot, and it stayed there until it fell on the floor. "That's it," he said. On Sunday he carried the basket over and set it beside the chair. By Wednesday, the shirts went in with a small flick, and the basket looked smaller.

qa.q: Where did Lakshman drop his shirt each evening?
qa.a: Lakshman dropped his shirt on the chair beside the cot.

qa.q: What did Lakshman realise after watching himself for three days?
qa.a: Lakshman realised that the shirts pile up because of the chair, not because the basket is too small, so he felt he had solved the puzzle.

qa.q: What alternative approach could Lakshman try, and why?
qa.a: Lakshman could set a fixed time each evening to empty the chair into the basket. A regular time turns the job into a habit.

qa.q: How might Ankita see the change?
qa.a: Ankita held her nose and laughed at first, so Ankita likely finds the tidier veranda a relief and may see her brother as more capable now.

grounding: A child notices the laundry basket always overflows, works out he leaves clothes on the chair, and moves the basket next to it.

subtype: Approach: noticing a chore keeps piling up and finding why [Revision]
passage: The heap around Pablo's laundry basket had spread onto the floor again, and his dad, Paulo, held up a sock with two fingers. "Washing day, amigo." Pablo started sorting and frowned. Most of the heap had not come from the basket at all. It came off his desk chair, where his jumper, jeans and school shirt landed every evening. The basket stood far away by the door, so the chair had become a second basket, and on washing day both piles crashed together into one overflowing mess. On Sunday Pablo dragged the basket across the room and wedged it beside the chair. That week, clothes dropped straight in. The next Saturday Paulo found one tidy load and a single stray sock under the bed.

qa.q: Where did Pablo's jumper, jeans and school shirt land every evening?
qa.a: They landed on his desk chair every evening.

qa.q: How did Pablo probably feel when he saw where most of the heap came from?
qa.a: He was probably puzzled at first and then a little embarrassed, and his frown shows he was working out why the pile kept growing.

qa.q: What would you change first if moving the basket had not helped, and why?
qa.a: Pablo could hang a hook on the chair back for clothes worn again, because then only truly dirty clothes would go in the basket.

qa.q: How does Pablo's change look to Paulo on the next washing day?
qa.a: Paulo finds one tidy load instead of a mess, so washing day is easier and he can see Pablo solved it himself 🙂

grounding: It shows a child noticing his clothes pile up on a chair, finding the reason and moving the basket beside the chair.

subtype: Approach: noticing a chore keeps piling up and finding why [Revision]
passage:
In Room 12 of the junior boys' hostel, Yash's laundry bag was always stuffed so full that the drawstring would not close. Devika ma'am, the warden, had tied it shut for him twice that month. On Thursday, during room check, she tapped his chair. "Why does your uniform live here?"
Yash looked. Every night he undressed sitting on that chair beside his bed, while the laundry bag hung on a hook far away by the door. The clothes piled up on the chair, and before laundry day he crammed the whole pile into the bag at once.
"The bag's in the wrong place," he said slowly. He asked if he could tie it to the back of his chair. The warden nodded. By the next laundry day the bag closed easily.

qa.q: Where did the laundry bag hang before Yash moved it?
qa.a: It hung on a hook far away by the door.

qa.q: How did Yash feel when he worked out why the bag kept overflowing?
qa.a: He seemed surprised and then pleased, speaking slowly as the reason became clear to him.

qa.q: What else could Yash try if clothes still pile up on busy nights?
qa.a: He could do a quick check of the chair before lights out each night, because a tiny daily step stops a big pile forming.

qa.q: How does the change look to Devika ma'am?
qa.a: The warden no longer has to tie his bag shut and can see he fixed the cause himself, so she is likely pleased.

grounding: It shows a child who notices his laundry keeps piling up, works out that clothes collect on his chair and moves the bag beside it.
